image_transform: Whole views; aspect-preserving fit into common tiles, padding and identical labels. No flip or content crop.
cadence: All recorded frames retained; 10 control frames per playback second; display only.

notes.text: Open and align above the orange can for a gentle touch-and-lift test; estimate alignment from both views.
Descend around the orange can with open fingers, correcting its small forward offset before closing.
Gently close on the orange can at its upper sides; next test a short lift and inspect retention.
Short vertical test lift of the orange can; inspect actual can motion rather than commanded gripper state.
Orange is visibly lifted. Test retention with a looser position-controlled grip close above the table; heaviness remains uncertain.
Orange slips under the loose grip; set it back down gently, then compare the blue can with the same test.
Clear the orange can and move above the blue can with fingers open for a comparable touch test.
Lower open fingers along the blue can's upper sides. Monitor centering before the test grasp.
Close gently around the blue can, then compare its retention during a short test lift.
Lift the blue can only six centimeters to test its physical response while keeping it close to the tabletop.
The rejected command moved nothing. Retry the stationary light-grip test, gradually opening to 0.8 and inspecting slip.
Blue released at 0.8, so that opening alone is inconclusive. Reposition for a slightly firmer light-grip test.
Apply a repeatable shallow closure of 0.75 to the blue can before checking lift retention.
Test whether the blue can follows a short lift with the shallow grip, observing slip against the fingers.
Blue follows the shallow-grip lift. Slightly reduce closure while raising a little more to check retention under the same gentle contact.
Blue remains retained under shallow closure and is the current light-can candidate. Secure it and raise above basket-rim height before transferring.
Carry the retained blue can horizontally toward the basket, maintaining rim clearance and the secure grasp.
Finish aligning the carried can over the basket opening, keeping the can upright and above the rim.
Open above the basket to release the blue candidate, then inspect that it falls inside rather than catches on the rim.
The blue can is falling within the opening. Keep the fingers clear and allow it to settle in the basket.
Blue has settled in the basket, but weight identification remains uncertain. Move clear toward the orange can for a comparable gentle retention test.
Align above the sideways orange can, turning the fingers across its cylindrical body rather than along its length.
Descend with open fingers to straddle the orange can's mid-body, accounting for its sideways position and hand-to-fingertip offset.
Close gradually across the sideways orange can's diameter for a gentle grasp; verify actual retention on the next lift.
Short vertical touch-test lift of orange at shallow closure, observing whether its body follows the fingers.
Orange also follows the shallow-contact lift. Secure this remaining candidate and raise it clear of the basket rim for placement.
Move the retained orange can above the center of the basket, keeping its horizontal body clear of the rim.
Release the orange can over the basket opening and observe its fall and clearance from the rim.
Withdraw open fingers vertically and let the orange can settle fully into the basket; inspect its position and the blue can beneath.
Orange appears supported above the basket interior by the other can. Regrasp orange to clear access, so only the selected can remains in the basket.
Regrasp the orange can across its body and begin a small clearance lift; verify it is captured before moving sideways.
Lift the regrasped orange can clear of the rim, then start moving to a temporary clear tabletop location to access the blue can.
Carry orange out of the basket to clear tabletop space, still securely held, while preserving clearance from the rim.
Lower the tilted orange can close to the tabletop for a gentle temporary set-down before removing blue from the basket.
Set orange down from minimal height and open fully, leaving it accessible while clearing blue from the basket.
Withdraw without dragging orange, then approach the basket from above to inspect and retrieve the blue can.
Center the open hand above the basket and inspect the blue can's resting orientation before retrieval.
Orient the fingers across the blue can's diagonal body and approach the basket interior cautiously for retrieval.
Refine alignment toward the visible blue body and rotate further across its axis, descending slowly within the basket.
The blue rim is now between the fingers. Close gradually for retrieval without moving farther into the basket.
